meanings.note: Understanding or surprise. Spoken French interj expression meaning 'ah', common in natural conversation.
aller + infinitive: tu vas l'agacer = you're going to annoy her
Je vais déjeuner. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to go'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'allé').
Imperative used to encourage. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to go'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'allé').

examples.trans: I'm going to have lunch twice.

meanings.note: S'asseoir sur une chaise. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to sit down, to seat'.
Transitive. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to sit down, to seat'.

examples.trans: A cushion to sit down on.

examples.text: Tu dois te balader avec un coussin pour t'asseoir.
examples.trans: You have to walk around with a cushion to sit on.

examples.text: On essayait de rester assis au fond.
examples.trans: We tried to stay sitting on the bottom.

meanings.note: avoir peur = to be afraid, avoir raison = to be right, avoir 40 ans = to be 40

meanings.en: helper verb of the passé composé
meanings.note: J'ai appelé = I called. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.

meanings.en: il y a = there is, there are
meanings.note: Fixed expression. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.
Avoir besoin de = to need. Masculine noun ('le besoin', plural 'les besoins') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'need'.

examples.text: Oui, oui. J'ai juste besoin d'un petit cours.
examples.trans: Yes, yes. I just need a little lesson.

meanings.note: Très bien = very well, fine. Invariable French adverb meaning 'well'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
C'est bien. Invariable French adverb meaning 'well'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Très bien. Et vous? Un thé?

meanings.note: bien sûr que + sentence = of course...

examples.text: Bien sûr que tu es fatiguée.
Bien sûr. Interflora, s'il vous plaît.

meanings.note: À bientôt = see you soon. Invariable French adverb meaning 'soon'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.trans: All right, I am breathing calmly.

meanings.note: determiner: ce soir = tonight, cette semaine = this week
pronoun: c'est = it is; tout ce que = all that

examples.text: Je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
Cette agence ne représente que des stars.
Magali, je dois voir la pièce de Koltès cette semaine.
examples.trans: Magali, I have to see the Koltès play this week.

meanings.note: D' before a vowel. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
le film de Tarantino = Tarantino's film
Also 'some': du sucre. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
French conjunction meaning 'so', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.

examples.text: Il est tard, donc je pars.
Donc, en fait, je ne suis pas vraiment réceptionniste.
examples.trans: So, actually, I'm not really a receptionist.

meanings.note: for things you can't count; de la (feminine)

examples.text: C'est du compost. Ça nourrit la terre.
examples.trans: It's compost. It feeds the earth.

meanings.note: Se détendre = to relax (oneself). Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation. Core French verb meaning 'to relax'.

examples.text: J'ai quelque chose pour se détendre.

meanings.note: entre toi et moi = between you and me

examples.text: Il n'y a rien entre nous.
S'il vous plaît. Il n'y a rien entre Mathias et moi, d'accord?
examples.trans: Please. There's nothing between Mathias and me, okay?

meanings.en: to come in, to go in
meanings.note: Passé composé with être. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to enter'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'entré').
Polite imperative. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to enter'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'entré').

examples.text: Entrez, je vous en prie, la porte est ouverte.
examples.trans: Come in, please, the door is open.

examples.text: Elle vient d'entrer dans le bureau de Mathias.
examples.trans: She just walked into Mathias's office.

meanings.note: The t is never pronounced. French conjunction meaning 'and', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.

examples.text: Et demain, tu déjeunes avec Audiard.
examples.trans: And tomorrow you're having lunch with Audiard.

meanings.note: also alone as an exclamation: Excellent!

examples.text: C'est une excellente nouvelle pour toute l'agence!
examples.trans: That is excellent news for the whole agency!

examples.text: Tu as fait un excellent travail sur ce contrat.
examples.trans: You did an excellent job on this contract.

meanings.note: Un fan de cinéma. Masculine noun ('le fan', plural 'les fans') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'fan'.

examples.text: Il faut penser aux vrais fans de la série.
examples.trans: We have to think of the real fans of the show.

examples.text: Elle est fan de cette actrice.
examples.trans: She's a fan of this actress.

examples.text: Excusez-moi, il faut penser aux vrais fans de la série.
examples.trans: Excuse me, we have to think of the real fans of the series.

meanings.note: Un fauteuil d'orchestre. Masculine noun ('le fauteuil', plural 'les fauteuils') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'armchair'.
Un fauteuil d'orchestre. Masculine noun ('le fauteuil', plural 'les fauteuils') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'armchair'.
pour l'instant = for the moment, for now
Un instant, s'il vous plaît. Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion. Standard masculine noun meaning 'instant, moment'.

examples.trans: Let us leave Juju alone for now.

meanings.note: J' before a vowel. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'I'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: Adverb: je veux juste. Invariable French adverb meaning 'just'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
Adjective. Invariable French adverb meaning 'just'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.trans: I just want to see Mathias.

examples.text: Oui, oui. J'ai juste besoin d'un petit cours.
examples.trans: Yes, yes. I just need a little lesson.

meanings.note: laisser quelqu'un voir = to let someone see
Laisse-moi = let me. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to leave'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'laissé').

examples.text: Laissez vos photos et votre CV ici.
examples.trans: Leave your photos and your CV here.

meanings.note: Masculine noun formed with the suffix '-age' (from Late Latin '-aticum') denoting an action, state, or collection. Standard masculine noun meaning 'massage (treatment)'.

examples.text: Un massage, ça fait du bien.
Réservez-moi un massage, s'il vous plaît.

meanings.note: Before the verb; m' before a vowel. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'me'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
ne... pas = not; ne... rien = nothing; ne... que = only; n' before a vowel

examples.text: Tarantino ne prendra pas Cécile. Problème d'âge.
examples.trans: Tarantino won't take Cécile. A problem with her age.

meanings.note: before the noun; nouvel before a vowel

Literature. Feminine noun ('la nouvelle', plural 'les nouvelles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'piece of news'.

Offrir un verre. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to give (as a present), to offer'.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'yes'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

meanings.note: second half of ne... pas; in speech ne is often dropped

examples.text: Tarantino ne prendra pas Cécile. Problème d'âge.

meanings.note: + infinitive. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'can, to be able to'.
conditional: tu pourrais, vous pourriez

examples.text: Rien n'est signé. On attend l'appel.
examples.trans: Nothing is signed. We're waiting for the call.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to settle'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'réglé').
Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to settle'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'réglé').

examples.text: Je n'en ai pas parlé à Gabriel. Mais règle ça, tu veux bien?
examples.trans: I haven't told Gabriel. But sort it out, will you?

savoir.gloss: to know; to know how to

meanings.note: Je ne sais pas = I don't know. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to know; to know how to'.
+ infinitive: savoir monter. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to know; to know how to'.

examples.trans: Do you know where he is?

meanings.note: j'ai senti un pied glisser = I felt a foot slip
Ça sent bon = it smells good. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to feel; to smell'.

examples.text: J'ai senti un pied glisser vers la tombe.
examples.trans: I felt one foot slip towards the grave.

meanings.note: Si tu veux = if you want. French conjunction meaning 'if', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.
answering a negative question: Aucune nouvelle? - Si!

examples.text: Si tu veux, on peut en parler demain matin.
examples.trans: If you want, we can talk about it tomorrow morning.

examples.text: Dis-moi tout de suite si le rôle t'intéresse.
examples.trans: Tell me right away if the role interests you.

meanings.note: Informal, does not change. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'great'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ce serait super si vous pouviez venir.
examples.trans: It would be great if you could come.

examples.text: J'ai trouvé un travail. Super, non?
examples.trans: I found a job. Great, isn't it?

meanings.note: Sur la table, sur la route. Core French preposition meaning 'on', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Sur haut-parleur = on speaker. Core French preposition meaning 'on', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Le livre est sur la table.
examples.trans: The book is on the table.

examples.text: Attention, tu arrives sur la route!
examples.trans: Careful, you're heading for the road!

meanings.note: Bien sûr = of course. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'sure'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Descriptive French adjective meaning 'sure'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'nervous strain, emotional tension'.

meanings.note: takes a singular verb: tout le monde est là

examples.text: Je suis vraiment désolée pour ce petit retard.
